name: Paper Flower
description: Native to the coastal regions of Brazil, Bougainvillea is an iconic tropical plant that produces spectacular displays of papery, tissue-like bracts in vivid magenta, purple, red, orange, white, or pink that can last for months. The true flowers are actually tiny and white, tucked inside the colorful bracts that steal the show. This vigorous climbing or sprawling plant can grow 20+ feet in ideal conditions but adapts well to containers with regular pruning, maintaining 3-6 feet indoors. The stems are armed with sharp thorns (handle with care!), and the plant has a Mediterranean temperament: it thrives on sun, heat, and strategic neglect. When stressed by drought and given maximum sun, it produces the most prolific color displays, creating walls of vibrant bracts.
toxicity: Pet safety unknown — not listed by the ASPCA, and we found no reports of it being toxic.
careInstructions: Water deeply, then let the soil dry out between waterings
Water freely in summer and sparingly in winter
Provide maximum direct sunlight - 6+ hours daily, more is better
Use a well-drained, slightly acidic, organically rich mix
Prune after flowering to maintain shape and control size - wear gloves!
Provide trellis or support for climbing growth habit
Fertilize every two weeks during the growing season, and stop in winter
Give it a cool winter rest - it drops most of its leaves, which it needs in order to flower. Move it somewhere warm and bright from March
commonProblems: Lack of color: Insufficient direct sunlight - needs maximum sun exposure
Green bracts instead of colored: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or shade
Leaf drop: Natural response to stress, environmental changes, or dormancy
Leggy growth with few flowers: Needs harder pruning and more sun
Thorns: Natural defense - always wear thick gloves when handling or pruning
Root rot: Overwatering - allow to dry significantly between waterings

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize every two weeks during the growing season, and stop in winter

whatsNormal: Drops most of its leaves during the cool winter rest — it needs that rest to flower.
The bright "petals" are bracts; the true flowers are small and white to yellow.
Sharp thorns — keep it out of busy walkways.

flags.note: Toxicity: no pet rating from ASPCA, NC State or the University of California — shown as "unknown". The University of California lists bougainvillea thorns as a skin irritant for people.
Low-nitrogen, high-phosphorus fertilizer type is from the original catalog; MOBOT only gives the every-two-weeks timing.
Winter watering interval (21 days) is our estimate — the sources only say to reduce watering from fall to late winter.

Changed: removed "drought stress encourages blooming" and the cactus-mix advice (both sources: rich, well-drained soil, water freely in summer); fertilizing monthly → every two weeks; added the cool winter rest it needs to flower (MOBOT).
